reference_sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ol.order_id) AS n_orders
FROM order_lines ol
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id
WHERE p.sku <> UPPER(TRIM(p.sku))
alternatives:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_orders
FROM orders o
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM order_lines ol
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id
  WHERE ol.order_id = o.order_id AND p.sku <> UPPER(TRIM(p.sku))
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS n_orders FROM order_lines WHERE product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM products WHERE sku <> UPPER(TRIM(sku)))

other_way.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_orders
FROM orders o
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM order_lines ol
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = ol.product_id
  WHERE ol.order_id = o.order_id AND p.sku <> UPPER(TRIM(p.sku))
)
other_way.tradeoff: EXISTS counts each order once without DISTINCT, but the join with COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) is shorter to read.
